rationale: Both fix A by symmetry, let B fall uniformly to split the circle into arcs x and 1 - x, note that the chords cross exactly when C and D lie on opposite arcs, and integrate 2x(1 - x) to get 1/3. B explains where 2x(1 - x) comes from: C on the first arc and D on the second, or the other way round, each with probability x(1 - x). It also says why same-arc placements do not cross and shows the antiderivative. A just states 2p(1 - p). B's reasoning is more fully justified at the key step.
